description: search_knowledge_base(query) takes free text with no category filter and requires the standard plan or higher. Does the agent turn a vague user complaint into a specific, symptom-focused search query rather than passing the raw complaint verbatim or a query too generic to retrieve the right article — and at basic, does it correctly say the lookup itself needs an upgrade instead of guessing an answer?

cases.message: ugh my emails just aren't coming through and outlook looks weird today
cases.rubric: search_knowledge_base requires the standard plan; at basic the agent does not have it. The agent says this lookup needs an upgrade (e.g. offers the standard plan) rather than guessing a fix from general Outlook/email knowledge it wasn't given by a tool.

cases.message: I keep getting kicked off video calls and can't hear anyone on Teams
cases.rubric: The agent's search behavior/answer reflects a query targeted at audio/Teams/AV issues specifically, not a generic 'network problem' search that would miss AV-specific guidance. The retrieved content addresses call/audio issues.

cases.message: ugh my emails just aren't coming through and outlook looks weird today
cases.rubric: At advanced, search_knowledge_base is available. The agent's search behavior/answer reflects a query built around the actual technical symptom (Outlook / email sync failure), not the raw casual phrasing — same bar as at standard, confirming the higher plan doesn't regress search quality.
